20 Critical Pros and Cons of Oil Energy
by Jordon Layne Jun 10, 2021
The process of bringing Oil to the surface for us to use is called oil drilling; this creates many Pros and Cons of Oil Energy. Before drilling for there are many geographical tests to be done to determine the size of the oil reservoirs. Oil can also be extracted from other resources, such as tar and shale. Once it is refined, Oil can be used to produce energy to power cities, run vehicles, and different types of machinery. Oil has been at the center of controversy for its effects on the environment. In this article, we will discuss the pros and cons of oil energy. Learn about most advantages, disadvantages, negatives, benefits that using oil energy is associated with.
Pros of Oil Energy
1. Oil Laid the Foundation for Renewable Energy.
Because of the technological advances of Oil over the years, we can now look into other sources of clean energy, such as solar and wind. The oil industry has laid the foundations of continuing efforts to find a clean source of energy. This can be attributed to the fact that our generation saw that we are using a source of energy that is not renewable and need to find alternatives for the long-term survival of our species. Researchers and leaders saw the need for a clean energy source that would be sustainable for future generations. As such, there is continued research and development into discovering and developing these sources of clean energy. In addition to the finite amount of Oil that we have (which spurred the need for finding other energy sources), we can also attribute Oil to the construction of wind turbines and solar panel arrays.
2. Oil is Cheap.
The energy that is produced by using Oil is cheap and relatively easy to transport over long distances. This makes it easy to provide rural and more remote areas where other energy sources may not be available. Even though it is a flammable resource, and there is some danger associated with it, Oil is relatively easy to transport because it is still just a liquid. Oil is cheaper than ever, considering the technological advances that we have made over the years in the industry. Oil is far less expensive to extract and refine today than it has been in the past. This can be attributed to the fact that we can extract Oil using offshore oil rigs and oil drilling in tar sands due to technological advances. Because through trial and error, we have perfected the means to extract and refine oil into usable products.
3. The Oil Industry Produces Jobs.
Due to the importance and scope of the oil industry, it provides millions of jobs to Americans. While these jobs may pay very well, there is a certain amount of danger involved, however. These jobs do pay very well, and there are thousands available, but that comes with a cost. Every day that someone works on transporting, drilling, or refining oil, they run the risk of serious bodily harm or not coming home at all.
4. Oil Goes a Long Way.
A small amount of Oil can yield a large amount of usable energy. This is a major plus considering how much Oil we consume daily and the fact that it is not a renewable resource. Even though we consume vast amounts of Oil daily, it simply shows how important it is to have a source of energy that can eventually replace Oil.
5. Oil is Cleaner than Coal.
Oil is cleaner than coal (but not as clean as renewable sources of energy like solar). Also, Oil is cheaper to convert into energy and use in today’s modern world. This has been a great boon to our environment, as it is not only cheaper but better for our planet.
6. Not Renewable, but Reliable.
Although Oil is not a renewable source of energy, it is a reliable one. Unlike solar energy, we do not rely on any other aspect of nature to continue drilling, refining, and using Oil (as long as the oil reservoirs are not dry). Because power stations are not reliant on sunlight or the amount of wind present, they can constantly work using Oil. This means that as long as a power station has Oil, it can continuously produce electricity for us to use.
7. Easy to Extract.
Because we have been doing this for so long, the process of extracting Oil is now relatively easy; especially compared to what it was many years ago. There are many ways now that we can extract Oil, and it is not only limited to drilling deep within the earth to acquire this resource. While drilling in the earth and offshore are still very viable options, and the most common, it is now possible to extract Oil by surface collection. These methods have been used for many years now and have proven themselves to be very viable ways to collect Oil.
8. Oil Energy is Adaptable.
Unlike other energy sources such as solar and wind, the energy produced by Oil can adapt to the consumer’s needs. As we know, there are times of the year that will either be much cooler or warmer than others. During these “peak seasons,” the need for electricity is higher than it would normally be. Renewable energy does not simply produce more just because we need it to. Still, energy from Oil can be used for these peak seasons to provide us with the necessary amount of energy to live comfortably.
9. Oil is Good for the Economy.
The economic aspect of our generation has roots in the oil industry. Because of this, other industries such as farming and agriculture have been able to thrive due to the use of Oil to power their vehicles and machines. In addition to using Oil as a source of energy, there are many other ways that we utilize this resource, such as the production of plastic and petroleum.
10. Oil is Global.
Oil is universal and can be accessed at a multitude of locations across the globe. This is not only great news for those regions that are more remote, but it removes the need for humans to fight over this resource (as much). And because it is easily transported through tankers and pipelines, we can all enjoy this resource and the quality of life it brings.
11. Substantial Dense Energy.
Oil is one of the few energy resources that are substantial and has a high energy density. Because of this, it is the resource of choice to power heavy machines and vehicles such as planes and factories. A small amount of oil has been proven to provide a lot of energy for us.
12. Ability to Safely Invest in Oil.
Because Oil is something that everyone currently needs to maintain their lives comfortably, any investors can confidently and safely invest in the oil industry. Oil is something that is a sound investment, and it isn’t going anywhere soon.
Cons of Oil Energy
1. Oil is non-Renewable.
We use the resources to extract and refine oil that is not renewable and run day run dry. This can lead to rationing the oil supply or eventually not being able to use Oil at all. The more oil consumed as a civilization today means less for future generations. This is one reason we must start to look for alternative energy sources, such as solar and wind. The majority of Oil is extracted from fossils that are found deep within the Earth, and although it is possible for more fossils to create Oil, that would take millions of years to do so. Although we can continue to use Oil for energy and other products for consumers right now, that will not last forever. It is a possibility that the oil reservoirs will run dry in the not too distant future. Decades ago, it was believed that around now would be the time that we would run out of Oil. Thankfully oil reservoirs are still being discovered, but there is no telling how long that can last.
2. Oil is Not Good for the Environment.
Oil is high in pollutants and is bad overall for the environment, more than just the amount of emissions that oil refineries put into the air. Due to refining oil, gasses such as Carbon Monoxide and Sulfur Dioxide are released into the atmosphere. These gases have been proven to be linked directly to allergies and diseases that plague the planet. I

The Pros and Cons of Crude Oil
The Pros and Cons of Crude Oil
Oil is the lifeblood of modern society. It has been more than a century since the late oil-boom when people traveled far and wide, drilling for oi l. Now, with modern technology, it has become easy to extract millions of barrels of oil from the depths of the earth.
In many countries, big corporations have started exploring and extracting oil from the seas. It is called black gold for a reason. The economies of several countries depend on oil industries.
Some of the pros and cons of crude oil are:
Advantages of Crude Oil:
1. Oil Energy is the Basis of all the Other Sources:
A nation’s development is gauged by the amount of oil they have, either through production at home or imports. While there are many renewable sources, oil is an everlasting source.
2. Oil Energy is Readily Available:
Though most of the machines that are emerging are electric, the primary component of many of those are oil-based. Due to the cars that are run by petrol and diesel, oil and its different products are used by the masses. It means that crude oil has a trickle-down effect, benefitting many industries.
3. It Produces More Energy When Burnt:
If you compare oil to other fuel sources, oil has a better burn rate. It is highly efficient, and the reason that oil is used by most industries. Moreover, people prefer diesel and petrol engine over CNG and electric. .
4. A Reliable Source of Energy
One thing that makes crude oil fuel more popular is its availability. You can find it anywhere you go.
Oil is processed to produce different fuels which can be refined to make a similar product. It is also more consistent in form than natural gas and electricity.
5. The Oil Boosts Economy
The oil boom has helped many countries with no apparent source of income turn into an economic hub. Countries such as UAE and Saudi Arabia, comprising of vast areas of deserts, have now become well-developed countries thanks to their oil resources. Wherever there has been a discovery of oil, prosperity has followed.
The Cons of Crude Oil
1. Limited Reserve
We have been using oil without any stop for more than a hundred years. There has been a vast number of digging and drilling going on daily for new sources. There are a lot of sources from which we can get oil, and still have plenty of untapped reserves.
The reality is that although we have used oil extensively, a time will come when the wells will run out of oil. It’s time that we looked for alternate sources.
2. Cause for Pollution
Oil is considered one of the leading reasons for global warming. The CO2 emission are high.  It is not only air pollution that crude oil affects, but land and sea pollution.
Each year thousands of barrels of crude oil in spilled in different parts of the world. It results in loss of life, and the whole ecosystem is disturbed.
Due to its use in mostly combustion engine. Machines release carbon dioxide and sulfur dioxide into the atmosphere. If a leak leads to inhalation, it could cause illnesses like allergies, lungs cancer, and skins diseases.
One solution is to regulate its flow through cast steel low-pressure check valves to prevent any leakage.
3. Fluctuation in Prices
The downside to having oil is that the whole economy is dependant on it, so if the rate of oil per barrel rise, so does everything else. It can cause problems for nations, especially those with a developing economy. It becomes challenging to control the prices of other commodities, and soon, the economy can spiral out of hand.
Conclusion
The pros and cons of oil energy depend upon how we use it. If we use it sparsely only for essentials, then it serves us well. Nonetheless, the way we have been exploiting these resources has caused more problems for us than we can handle.
It is high time we explore other venues as well. This way, we will be able to counter the global warming issue as well as be safe from any potential energy crisis as it is entirely possible that one day we will run out of oil.
